function.mechanism: Provides yellow coloration/fluorescence and serves as precursor of FMN/FAD coenzymes involved in cellular redox and energy metabolism.
common_food_categories: Foods generally (US color additive use under 21 CFR 73.450)

adi.basis: EFSA ANS Panel (2013) concluded no need for a numerical ADI for E101(i)/(ii) at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Riboflavin (E101(i)) and riboflavin-5'-phosphate sodium (E101(ii)) were not of safety concern at currently reported uses and use levels.

concerns.summary: A recent rat study using high-dose neonatal riboflavin (100 mg/kg) reported metabolic and mitochondrial remodeling; relevance to routine food-additive exposure is uncertain.
Human observational findings summarized by NIH are mixed/inconclusive for cancer endpoints and do not show a consistent harmful association at dietary intake levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2013 re-evaluation found no safety concern at reported uses and no numerical ADI needed.
JECFA lists ADI as not limited.
NIH ODS reports no established UL because adverse effects from high riboflavin intakes have not been reported in available data.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined exposure estimates reached up to 1.3 mg/kg bw/day in high-level toddlers/children; with no numerical EFSA ADI and JECFA ADI 'not limited', routine exceedance determination is not applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Riboflavin is a naturally occurring vitamin with broad regulatory acceptance (EFSA approved, FDA GRAS, JECFA ADI not limited), and no credible evidence of harm at normal food-additive exposure levels.
key_factors: EFSA: no safety concern at reported uses and no numerical ADI needed
FDA: GRAS affirmation under 21 CFR 184.1695 and color use under 21 CFR 73.450
No riboflavin entry found in IARC classified agents list
